dossier.summary: Group of 14 dental clinics across two states.

data.notes:
Tidewell Dental Group (tidewell.example). 14 dental clinics across two states, about 320 staff. Champion: Ines Calder, Chief Operating Officer. Shared link goes to the operations leadership.
Calls: Oct 12 (Ines Calder, Marcus Webb, Rosa Delgado, Elena Park) and Oct 22 (Ines Calder, Elena Park).
Quotes, Oct 12. Ines Calder, Chief Operating Officer: "A referral goes out the door and we never see it again. The patient tells us three weeks later that nobody called." Rosa Delgado, Regional Clinic Manager: "My front desk keeps referrals in a shared inbox and a binder. When someone is off, the binder wins."
Quote, Oct 22. Marcus Webb, Director of Patient Access: "New patients fill in a paper form on arrival. That is ten minutes of the first appointment gone."
Numbers from Rosa's September referral log for Riverside and Eastgate, shared Oct 20: 212 specialist referrals sent, 61 with no confirmed appointment after 14 days; front desks spend about 9 hours a week chasing referrals per clinic; 38 percent of new patients complete their forms before arrival.
Pilot sites: Riverside and Eastgate clinics, 6 front-desk staff. Scheduling system is read-only for the pilot. SSO through Google Workspace. Weekly 30-minute review with Rosa and Anika.
Out until year one: the other 12 clinics, the patient text-message reminders, insurance pre-checks, billing.
Wants: referrals with a confirmed appointment within 14 days up from 71 percent to 88 percent; front-desk time chasing referrals down to 4 hours a week per clinic or less; 80 percent of new patients complete forms before arrival; 5 of 6 front-desk staff use the tracker every working day. Today none of the front-desk staff use a shared tracker.
Stakeholders: Ines Calder (sponsor, 30 minutes a week); Rosa Delgado (pilot lead, 2 hours a week); Marcus Webb (intake forms, 1 hour a week); Elena Park, Compliance Lead (privacy review, 3 hours in weeks 1 and 2).
Dates: proposal sent Oct 29, valid for 30 days. Scoping call Nov 5. Privacy review answers Nov 9. Proposal version 2 on Nov 11. Decision on the pilot Nov 13. Kickoff at Riverside Nov 16. Pilot Nov 16 to Dec 16. Weekly reviews Nov 23, Nov 30, Dec 7 and Dec 14. Readout Dec 17. Decision on year one Dec 21.
data.offer:
Pilot: 30 days at up to two clinics, fixed fee $3,600. It covers the scheduling connector, intake form setup, training, four weekly reviews and the readout. The pilot fee is credited in full against year one if the customer signs by Dec 31, 2026.
Year one: up to 14 clinics from January 2027, $41,000 a year, billed annually. Onboarding for every additional clinic is included.
Prices in US dollars, before tax. Proposals are valid for 30 days.

data.problem_close: The referrals are sent. They are not tracked after that. Each clinic keeps its own record, so nobody can see which ones are open.
data.scope_lead: One referral tracker and one digital intake form for the front desk, starting at two clinics. The platform reads from your scheduling system; nothing is written back.
scope_in: Read-only connector to the scheduling system at Riverside and Eastgate
Referral tracker with an owner and a next step on every open referral
Digital new-patient form, sent before the first visit
Weekly 30-minute review with Rosa and Anika
data.scope_close: If the pilot passes, year one extends the same setup to all 14 clinics, with the Riverside team training the next ones.
data.pilot_lead: Nov 16 to Dec 16 at Riverside and Eastgate with Rosa Delgado's front-desk teams. Four criteria, measured against September.

criteria.name: Referrals with a confirmed appointment within 14 days
Front-desk hours a week spent chasing referrals
New patients who complete forms before arrival
Front-desk staff using the tracker each working day

data.pass_rule: The pilot passes when three of the four criteria are met across the last two weeks, Dec 3 to Dec 16. If it does not pass, there is no year-one commitment and the pilot fee is the only cost.
data.timeline_lead: Seven weeks from the scoping call to a decision on year one. The privacy review and the connector run in parallel so the pilot can start on Nov 16.
data.timeline_note: Diamonds are single-day events. The Dec 21 decision keeps the pilot credit inside the year.
